positions.subject: q:energy/loosen-oil-production-limits
positions.summary: Hilton's $3 gas plan proposes suspending the Low Carbon Fuel Standard, reformulation requirements and other refinery regulations, taking steps to increase California oil production, and suspending enforcement of SBX1-2 and ABX2-1.

citations.quote: Suspend the Low Carbon Fuel Standard (LCFS), reformulation requirements, and other extreme and unnecessary refinery regulations: These compliance costs add roughly 40 cents per gallon.

Additional deregulation measures, including immediate steps to increase California oil production and the suspension of enforcement of SBX1-2 and ABX2-1, could reduce prices even further, by up to 25¢ per gallon.

positions.subject: q:immigration/expand-cooperation-federal-enforcement
positions.summary: Asked at the Sept. 30 CNN debate whether he would help carry out mass deportations despite state limits on cooperation, Hilton did not say whether he would change the sanctuary law; he said his goal is to lower the temperature and pledged to prioritize removing dangerous criminals.

citations.quote: On Wednesday night, he dodged questions on whether he would undo the state’s sanctuary law limiting police cooperation with immigration agents and direct California officers to assist in Trump’s campaign.

Asked whether he would assist in helping the Trump administration carry out mass deportations despite state laws that limit cooperation with federal law enforcement, Hilton noted his own background as a child of European immigrants and said his goal is “to lower the temperature on this whole question.” He pledged to protect “legal immigrant communities" and prioritizing removing “dangerous criminals.”

positions.subject: q:taxes/lower-top-income-tax-rates
positions.summary: Hilton's platform proposes no state income tax on the first $150,000 of income and a single 8% rate on income above $150,000.

citations.quote: Income above $150,000 would be taxed at a simple 8% rate.
California has the highest income tax rate in the nation. The highest statewide sales tax rate. The highest gas tax.

positions.subject: q:transportation/high-speed-rail-funding
positions.summary: Hilton's spending plan says he will cancel state funding for high-speed rail, and at the Sept. 30 debate he named canceling high-speed rail as a source for his tax cuts.

citations.quote: Cancel state funding for high-speed rail.

announced a unified commitment to stop future taxpayer-funded payments for California's High-Speed Rail project unless the state can prove the current project complies with Proposition 1A — the measure approved by voters in 2008.

"The quickest way to get more money in people's pockets is for the government to take less out. That's what I'm going to be doing, and it's not coming from the budgets he describes. You know what it's coming from? Canceling high-speed rail," Hilton said.
